## Features

| Feature | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| 🎙 **Spoken answers** | A 60–90 second, say-it-out-loud version of an answer, with a speak-first practice timer, a *Listen* button and likely follow-up questions. Every question in every guide has one. The Behavioral STAR answers (and Product Management Q53–56) are **illustrative first-person samples** — replace the scenarios with your own stories. |
| 📚 **Official docs links** | Up to three links to official documentation under each answer (about 82% of questions get a specific page, the rest get a *start here* link for the guide's main docs). Links were curated by hand without live verification from the authoring environment; run `node tools/check_links.mjs` to check them and report dead ones. |
| 🌳 **Decision trees** | Eleven click-through troubleshooting trees (pod won't start, high latency, 5xx spike and more) in [`decision_trees.html`](https://interviewhub.eknathalabs.com/decision_trees.html), each leaf linking to the relevant questions. |
| 🖨 **Printable PDFs** | One print-optimised PDF per guide in [`pdf/`](pdf/), including the spoken answers and docs links. Rebuild with `python3 tools/build_pdfs.py` (needs Playwright). Any guide also prints cleanly from the browser (`print.css`). |
| 🗺 **Diagrams** | 335 inline SVG diagrams (flows, layers, comparisons) on selected questions across 19 guides — about 11% of questions, not all. Generated from small hand-written specs in `diagrams/<guide>.js` by `diagrams.js`; theme-aware, work offline and print in the PDFs. The behavioral guide has none. |
| 🌐 **Multi-language UI** | Interface in English, हिन्दी, తెలుగు, தமிழ், ಕನ್ನಡ and മലയാളം (language picker in the header, remembered per browser). **Only the interface is translated** — questions and answers stay in English. The translations were written by the maintainer's tooling and have **not** been reviewed by native speakers; corrections are welcome. |
| 📱 **Desktop and mobile friendly** | Responsive layout (`responsive.css`) for phones, tablets and desktops: no horizontal scroll on any page at 390 px and 1280 px (checked with a headless browser; not yet tested on physical devices). |
| 👁 **Visitor count** | Anonymous visit counter on the home page (see Privacy below). |
| 📄 **Resume → questions mapper** | Paste your resume, get the questions you are most likely to be probed on, ranked by overlap with your own skills. Runs 100% in your browser — nothing is uploaded. Open [`resume_mapper.html`](https://interviewhub.eknathalabs.com/resume_mapper.html). |
| ▶ Interview mode | Flashcard drill — random question, reveal answer, Got it / Missed it scoring, progress bar |
| 🔍 Full-text search | Find any command, concept or error message inside each guide |
| 🏷 Category filters | Filter by subtopic within each guide |
| ☾ Dark mode | One-click toggle everywhere; remembered across sessions |
| 📴 Offline-ready | Pure HTML/JS — no build step, no server, no network calls |

**About the question set:** each guide includes at least 50 additional *commonly asked* questions, each with a spoken answer. They are written from common interview themes; they are **not** sourced from verified real interviews and carry no company tags. The worked examples in the Behavioral STAR guide are illustrative, not real stories — use your own.

**Privacy:** no login, no ads, no cookies, no personal data. The portal home page shows an anonymous visit counter (`counter.js`): it makes one request to the counter service per browser per day, which — like any web server — sees that request's IP address. Switch provider or turn it off with one line (`PROVIDER = 'off'`). Dark-mode and study progress are stored in your browser's `localStorage` only.

## Run locally

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8000      # from this folder, or just open index.html in a browser
```

## Maintaining the content

Counts in this README are generated from the guides themselves, so they cannot drift.

```bash
node tools/extract.mjs        # reads every guide's question data -> data/questions.json, prints real counts
node tools/check_spoken.mjs   # validates spoken answers (question exists, 130–215 words ≈ 60–90 s)
node tools/sync_readme.mjs    # rewrites the guides table and headline count above
node tools/build_mapper.mjs   # rebuilds the offline index inside resume_mapper.html
# adding questions in bulk: write newq/<guide>.json, then  tools/addq.sh <guide>  (updates counts, spoken answers and checks)
```

Run all four after editing a guide or adding spoken answers. Requires Node 18+.

### Adding a spoken answer

1. Open `spoken/<guide>.js` (guide key = file name without `_interview_guide.html` / `_guide.html`). For a guide with no spoken file yet, create it and add `<script src="spoken/<guide>.js"></script>` followed by `<script src="spoken.js"></script>` before `</body>` in that guide.
2. Add an entry keyed by the question number:

   ```js
   37: { a: `Spoken answer in first person…`, f: ['Likely follow-up 1', 'Likely follow-up 2'] },
   ```

3. Shape every answer for speech, not for reading: **conclusion first (~10 s) → mechanism (~25 s) → a concrete example or command (~25 s) → trade-off or caveat (~15 s)**. Aim for 140–200 words. No bullet lists, no tables.
4. Run `node tools/check_spoken.mjs`.
